analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB write is caused by decoding edge macroblocks without bounds checks against actual plane dimensions. In bink_decode_plane(), block loops use bw/bh rounded up to block counts, and for SCALED_BLOCK+FILL_BLOCK it calls fill_block_tab[0](dst, v, stride, 16), which writes a full 16-byte row width for 16 rows (via fill_block16_c memset(16)). On right/bottom edge blocks where frame width/height are not multiples of 16 (chroma) or 8 (luma), dst can point to the last valid column and the 16-byte write overruns the allocated frame buffer. The bug is missing clipping/edge handling before full-block writes.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger with a crafted Bink frame that makes bink_decode_plane() process a boundary block as SCALED_BLOCK with sub-type FILL_BLOCK (or other full-size unbounded block writes), while decoded plane dimensions are not exact block multiples. Data flow: fuzzer packet -> decode_frame() allocates frame via ff_get_buffer -> bink_decode_plane() iterates rounded-up bw/bh and writes full blocks at dst. For edge blocks, writing 16x16 (or 8x8 similarly) without restricting to remaining width/height causes heap-buffer-overflow; PoV shows write at end of a 512-byte plane buffer.
